Two piece of ginger about the size of your pointer & middle finger sliced into coin size pieces 3.    Honey (about 1 cup or Your preferences) Optional: ~1 tsp. ground cinnamon In a 12-16 oz. jar combine lemon slices and sliced ginger. Pour honey over it slowly. ⭐️Sore Throats, Snuffles & Sneezes⭐️ Who else makes a gorgeous fresh juice bursting with goodies whenever you or your kids are going down with a sore throat, sniffle or sneeze? Fresh juices have always been a trusty winner in my household, which you will learn all about in my Little Hero stories in The Good Stuff.  And just this week it’s helped us all nip a winter lurgy in the bud before it took hold - maybe we were just lucky?  Fresh juices are packed with Vitamin A & C as well as polyphenols to nourish the immune system. I always add a big chunk of fresh ginger root which has natural antibacterial and antiviral properties and gives it a lovely zing.  I don’t put the lemon through the juicer as it makes the juice a bit bitter, so just squeeze in the juice and stir in at the end. And you really don’t need a fancy juicer, I’ve had mine for over a decade and it cost less than £100.  Kids love these juices too and any leftovers you can freeze into soothing ice lollies.  They don’t give a sugar hit as much as shop bought juices as they retain some fibre, especially if you include plenty of carrot or other veg like cucumber, celery or kale.  My current favourite, which makes a big juice for 3 people (but could stretch to 4/5 people) is a combo of: 1 x 🍊 4 x 🍎 4 x 🥕 1 x 🍋 ➕Thumb size knob of ginger  What do you love adding to your juices? SURGERY UPDATE: Hopefully tiktok does not take this post down. Wanting to raise awareness of the surgery I had yesterday!  Straight after theatre the doctor informed me my tonsils were extremely grotty from the previous infections ive had & they really needed to come out. I was really doubting getting this surgery done as all I had personally heard was horror stories and no wonder… In recovery I woke up panicked to the worst breathing ever (stridor) i had to have a number of puffs of my inhaler which ive not had to have for many months now. Luckily my breathing rectified. I was in absolute agony with my throat and needed several different types of pain relief both in recovery & surgery itself.  Due to the amount of pain relief id had and the general anaesthetic itself, i then went into urinary retention & couldnt pee again! Those that know me well know i had a suprapubic catheter in my abdomen for 3 years. I got the sacral nerve stimulator and since having that device i was able to pee myself and never had any problems since it was inserted in sept. Until yesterday when i needed to use a catheter because i couldnt pee.  Im still on a lot of pain meds currently but im hoping theyll let me home later and theyll discharge me with pain relief, difflam mouthwash etc. I could only eat a scoop of icecream and a yoghurt yesterday & it took me over an hour to eat both.  All i can say is its been a long 2 days already and im not looking forward to the rest of my recovery.  #tonsils #tonsilremoval #tonsilectomy #tonsilectomyrecovery #sorethroat #infections #hospital #surgery

This exercise is GREAT for a bit of vocal rehab 💪 Our vocal folds need to slam together to create sound…. 😱 You'll be surprised what "ANGINA" actually means 🫀 Doctor Azmain explains 👇 You probably know that angina refers to a type of chest pain - usually due to exertion or exercise. There's another type called Prinzmetal angina due to coronary vasospasm. But Vincent's angina is completely different - it refers to a type of tonsillitis! That's because "angina" means "strangling" in Latin, so angina pectoris is "strangling of the chest" but tonsillitis can cause a strangling sensation of the throat too. This Is Why You Shouldn’t Have Your Tonsils Out Unless You Really Need It #infection  Having your tonsils removed, also known as a tonsillectomy, can be a beneficial medical procedure in certain situations. This surgery is typically recommended when individuals experience recurring or severe issues related to their tonsils. Here are some reasons why someone might consider having their tonsils removed: Recurrent Tonsillitis: Frequent and severe episodes of tonsillitis, which can cause throat pain, fever, and difficulty swallowing, may necessitate tonsil removal. Chronic Sore Throat: If persistent sore throats are impacting your quality of life, removing the tonsils might offer relief. Breathing Problems: Enlarged tonsils can obstruct the airway, leading to breathing difficulties, especially during sleep. Sleep Apnea: Tonsillectomy can be part of the treatment plan for obstructive sleep apnea, a condition characterized by interrupted breathing during sleep. Snoring: Loud snoring due to enlarged tonsils can disrupt your sleep and that of those around you. Frequent Strep Throat: Recurrent strep throat infections may prompt the removal of tonsils to prevent further complications. Peritonsillar Abscess: In some cases, a painful abscess around the tonsils may require surgical drainage and subsequent tonsillectomy. Difficulty Swallowing: Enlarged tonsils can make swallowing uncomfortable or challenging. Tonsil Stones: Chronic tonsil stones, which are calcified debris in the tonsil crypts, can be a source of discomfort and bad breath. Cancer Concerns: In rare cases, if there are suspicions of cancerous growth in the tonsils, removal may be recommended for diagnostic and treatment purposes. Remember, the decision to have a tonsillectomy should be made in consultation with a medical professional who can assess your specific condition and needs. This is Gonna Do Wonders for Bad Breath #procedure Tonsil stones, also known as tonsilloliths, are small, calcified masses that can develop in the crevices of the tonsils at the back of the throat. These stones are typically composed of debris, such as dead cells, mucus, and food particles, that become trapped and accumulate in the tonsil crypts. Tonsil stones can vary in size and are often whitish or yellowish in color. They may cause symptoms like bad breath, sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and ear pain. While they are generally harmless, they can be bothersome and occasionally lead to discomfort. Treatment options range from at-home remedies like gargling with saltwater to more severe cases requiring surgical removal of the tonsils. It's essential to consult a healthcare professional if you experience persistent symptoms or discomfort related to tonsil stones. #TonsilStones #Tonsilloliths #OralHealth #BadBreath #ThroatHealth #TonsilCrypts #SoreThroat #EarPain #OralHygiene #HealthConditions #ThroatDiscomfort #AtHomeRemedies #OralCare #TonsilHealth #OralHealthcare #MedicalAdvice #TonsilRemoval #Symptoms #DentalHealth #HealthAwareness #WellnessJourney #fyp #fypシ #medicine

2015, a few days/weeks before Layla's 9th Birthday her hip started hurting. She would start off some days 'ok' & come out of school 'dragging' her leg behind. She complained of many #symptoms pain being the one obvious one. Then #tonsillitis then changes in feelings across her body, tummy ache, headaches, feeling 'ill'. We were referred for a scan, something I had to fight for as Layla's attendance dropped, school work suffered, her mood and fun, outgoing active personality disappeared. She was diagnosed in March with #crps met what we now know is the criteria for #ehlersdanlos HOWEVER every symptom for #pandas #encephalitis was met in the 12 months following her first #strepinfection AS SOON as someone mentioned it may be #complexregionalpainsyndrome EVERYOTHER symptom was dismissed. Speak up, ask for help if you feel you aren't being heard. As we approach our baby girls 18th Birthday, I'm reminded of that first big relapse, the one we were told was 'the excitement of xmas'. What a crock of 💩 💩 💩.  It was #strep more than likely. 1 #diagnosis does not mean you can't have another. Story time because I can neither speak for that long or have the energy  So started getting a sore throat on Thursday afternoon. No biggie I gwt tonsillitis at least once a year and have done for best part of a decade.  Friday lost my ability to speak, much to partners pure enjoyment. Don't think he's ever known me to be so quiet. Started to struggle with swallowing. Managed 3 sips of tea and was in eye-watering pain  the rest of the day and through the night. Parenting was tough.  Saturday we called 111. I couldn't speak at all, couldn't swallow at all. Dehydrated and in absolute agony. Arrived at A&E at 6:10pm and was instantly put on antibiotics, fluids and IV pain meds. Sit around waiting for ENT Dr to have a look. Got seen by ENT at 9ish. Bloods came back high infection markers, getting admitted, wanna aspirate my tonsils in morning.  Managed a full brew, 200ml of juice and 20ml of ibuprofen solution because they couldn't IV that. Slowly but surely the pain is easing. The swelling of the throat and tonsils has not.  Anyway, I'm in the shitter when I get home because I can't admit he was right... Again... What's small, yet very powerful? 💥 Tech Billionaire? 🤓 Probably.  💊Paracetamol!  (or acetaminophen of you're from the US)  I often hear that patients have taken too many paracetamol because their pain was so bad. If they've taken too many for their weight, they end up in A&E for bloods and sometimes treatment.  If  you're aged 16+ and weigh over 50 kilos you can  take  2 paracetamol (1 gram) up to 4 times a day. (No more than 4 doses in 24 hours)  Please read the labels. Many cold and flu remedies contain paracetamol. These medicines include  Cocodamol, Lemsip and  nightnurse. ‼️Be aware! A small dose over the recommended limit can do irreparable damage to your liver ‼️ Some 'designer' brands contain caffeine, pretty colours and other good stuff but paracetamol is the same where ever you buy it from.💷 (Aldi and Lidl are probably the cheapest). 💡Top Tip. 💡Keep a note of when  when you take your medications to avoid taking too much, too soon. FAST TRACK APPOINTMENTS WITH PHARMACY FIRST SERVICE The Pharmacy First Service offers quick access to treatment for conditions like impetigo, infected insect bites, otitis media, shingles, urinary tract infections (UTIs), sore throats, and acute sinusitis. Pharmacists can provide medications such as antibiotics, antivirals, or over-the-counter treatments without needing a GP appointment. Red flags for referral include systemic symptoms, rapid spread of infection, severe or persistent pain, or fever. Specific criteria apply depending on the condition and patient age, with referrals to a GP if symptoms are severe or prolonged, particularly for young children or immunocompromised patients.
